root_shock.label: AI data-center electric-load expansion
root_shock.mechanism: Accelerating AI and large-computing deployments increased committed electric load in major U.S. data-center regions, advancing grid interconnection, utility-structure, and facility structural-steel procurement before the dated market trigger.
causal_chain: AI compute deployments increase committed data-center electricity load
large-load interconnections advance transmission and utility-structure procurement
data-center and grid construction raises fabricated structural-metal backlog

evidence.summary: DBM Global reported backlog growth and visibility into 2027 and 2028, explicitly identifying sustained AI-infrastructure and technology demand among the supporting end markets.
Arcosa reported record utility-and-related-structures backlog of $648.1 million, up 49% from the start of 2026.
DOE's LBNL-backed report estimated U.S. data-center electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023 and projected 325 to 580 TWh by 2028, with AI applications identified as a driver of load growth.

EIA forecast rapid ERCOT and PJM electricity-demand growth and tied the regional increase to proposed data centers and other large facilities, including 14% ERCOT demand growth in 2026 as projects came online.
NERC's FERC filing documented rapidly increasing data-center-type loads and the resulting need for grid planning, reliability analysis, information sharing, and large-load integration work.
